title: Fabrication of Engineered Vascular Flaps Using 3D Printing Technologies
protocol: Create a 3D computer model of the desired vascular scaffold shape using CAD software or download a 3D file from online repositories.
Design a cylinder with an inner diameter of 0.9 mm, an outer diameter of 2 mm, and a height of 18 mm.
Add radial fenestrations with a diameter of 0.22 mm alongside the cylinder wall.
Create a mold for the scaffold using 3D design software and export it as an .STL file.
Add a funnel to the design to ease filling of the mold later.
Import the .STL file into slicing software for an FDM 3D printer.
Slice the model with a layer height of 0.1 mm, and export it as .gcode or send directly to the 3D printer.
3D print the mold on an FDM 3D printer equipped with a 0.25 mm nozzle using water-soluble BVOH filament.
Store the printed molds in a vacuum chamber until use.
Weigh 350 mg of PLLA and transfer to a 20 mL glass vial.
Weigh 350 mg of PLGA and add to the glass vial containing PLLA.
Measure 10 mL of 1,4-dioxane and transfer to the glass vial using a glass pipette.
Add a small magnetic stir bar to the glass vial.
Place the glass vial inside a hot water bath heated to 70 °C.
Mix overnight until all polymers dissolve fully.
Store the solution in an airtight glass container until use.
Fill BVOH molds with the PLLA:PLGA polymer solution using a positive displacement pipette.
Measure 30 μL of the polymer solution and fill in the mold.
Keep adding the polymer solution until the funnel of the mold is entirely filled.
Centrifuge the mold at 100 × g for 2 min.
Top up the mold with an additional 20 μL of the polymer solution to ensure complete filling.
Freeze the filled molds at -80 °C for at least 30 min.
Remove solvent from the molds by lyophilizing them overnight.
Disinfect the PLLA:PLGA vascular scaffolds by immersing them in 70% ethanol for 30 min.
Wash the scaffolds 3x 5 min with PBS.
Mix 500 μl of stock fibronectin solution (1 mg/ml) with 9.5 ml of PBS to prepare a dilution of 50 µg/ml human fibronectin in PBS.
Immerse the disinfected vascular scaffolds in this fibronectin solution and incubate them at 37 °C for 60 min to allow for protein adsorption.
Rinse the scaffolds with PBS to remove the unbound fibronectin.
Store these coated scaffolds at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
Dissolve 5.495 g of Na2HPO4, 1.55 g of NaH2PO4, and 30 mg of NaCl in 50 ml of deionized water to prepare a 10x stock of phosphate buffer.
Combine 1 part of the 10x phosphate buffer with 9 parts of deionized water to prepare a 10-fold dilution of the 10x phosphate buffer.
Combine 900 µL of stock rhCollMA solution with 100 µL of 10x phosphate buffer.
Dilute the neutralized rhCollMA solution to a concentration of 10 mg/mL using 1x phosphate buffer.
Prepare a 1.6% (w/v) solution of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) in phenol red-free DMEM by dissolving 160 mg of PEO in 10 mL of DMEM.
Add 20 mg of lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP) to the PEO solution to obtain a 0.2% (w/v) LAP solution.
Sterilize the PEO-LAP solution by filtering it through a 0.22 µm filter.
Store the sterilized PEO-LAP solution at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
Mix the diluted neutral rhCollMA solution with the PEO-LAP solution in a 1:1 ratio to obtain the final bioink solution.
Use pipetting to mix the solutions while avoiding air bubbles.
If air bubbles are introduced, centrifuge the solution at 2,000 × g for 30 seconds.
After centrifugation, remix the bioink solution to ensure homogeneity.
Prepare gelatin granular support material.
In a biological safety cabinet, divide the contents of one 2 g tube of lyophilized support material into two sterile 50 mL conical tubes.
Add 40 mL of cold (4 °C) phenol-red free DMEM to each tube.
Vortex vigorously until all the lyophilized support material dissolves.
Let the resulting slurry sit at 4 °C to allow the support material to rehydrate.
Degas the support material in a vacuum chamber for 30 min to reduce bubbles.
Centrifuge the support material at 2,000 × g for 5 min.
Ensure that the material is at the bottom of the tube and the supernatant is clear.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without aspirating the support material at the bottom.
Transfer approximately 4 mL of the prepared, compacted support material into each well of a 12-well plate using a positive displacement pipette.
Tap the well plate on a hard surface to force the support material to spread evenly in the well.
Place the well plate with the support material on a cooled bioprinter stage or at 4 °C until its use.

Prepare endothelial cell medium according to the manufacturer's instructions by mixing the basal medium with its corresponding medium kit component, including an antibiotic solution, fetal bovine serum, and endothelial cell growth supplements.

Combine 500 mL of low-glucose DMEM, 58 mL of fetal bovine serum, 5.8 mL of non-essential amino acids (NEAA), 5.8 mL of glutamine substitute, 5.8 mL of 1 M HEPES, and 5.8 mL of penicillin-streptomycin-nystatin solution to prepare dental pulp stem cell medium.

Mix a suspension containing 2 × 10^6 ZsGreen1-expressing human adipose microvascular endothelial cells (HAMEC-ZsGreen1) and 6 × 10^6 dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) in 10 mL of endothelial cell medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 4 min to obtain a cell pellet.
Aspirate the supernatant medium.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of rhCollMA bioink prepared previously (containing PEO-LAP) to obtain a bioink with a total cell concentration of 8 × 10^6 cells per 1 mL of bioink.
Transfer the cells-bioink mixture into printing cartridges.
Fit a 0.22 mm internal diameter needle to a 3 mL amber printing cartridge.
Place the cartridge in a 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer 1 mL of the cells-bioink mixture to the printing cartridge by filling it from the top.
Use a positive displacement pipette to reduce bubbles.
Install the printing cartridge in the appropriate tool at the bioprinter.
Create a 3D CAD design for the bioprinted microvascular network.
Sketch a 2D pattern of a 4 mm square containing a 2 mm diameter circular channel in its center.
Extrude the sketch by 4 mm to obtain a 4 mm x 4 mm x 4 mm cube with a central channel.
Export this object as an .STL file.
Import a 12-well plate .STL template into the solid modeling tab in the bioprinter slicing software.
Place it in the designated area of the virtual print bed.
Import the .STL file of the cube shape into the solid modeling tab in the bioprinter slicing software.
Click on the use external slicer checkbox | configure slicer under the object properties section.
In the popup window, choose a rectilinear pattern for the fill pattern.
Type 30% in the fill density.
Click accept.
Place a copy of the cube shape in each desired virtual well by clicking on the cube and moving it using the mouse.
Create new material settings for rhCollMA bioink in the bioprinter slicing software.
Click the add material button and choose the material's settings for printing.
Type 2 psi in the pressure box.
Type 20 mm/s in the speed box.
Assign line width of 0.24 mm and line height of 0.24 mm to the cube object.
Set acceleration value to 400 mm/s².
Click on the rhCollMA material from the materials section to assign it to the cube shape.
In the bioassembly tab, click on the send print job button to send the print job to the bioprinter.
Load the printing cartridge loaded with cellular bioink into the 3 mL ambient pneumatic dispense tool of the bioprinter.
Set the print bed temperature to 4 °C by clicking on the cool button under the Control-Heating/Cooling tab.
Load the plate with the support bath onto the printer bed.
Click on the print job sent in Step 6.7 and click start | go to begin the print job.
Expose the well-plate to a 405 nm light source with an intensity of 3 mW/cm² for 30 seconds to initiate crosslinking of the rhCollMA bioink.
Incubate the well plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for at least 20 minutes until all the support bath melts.
Gently aspirate the liquified support bath and replace it with endothelial cell medium.
Incubate the constructs at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until use in further steps.
Place a fibronectin-coated PLLA:PLGA vascular scaffold in the main channel of the bioprinted structure immediately after support material removal.
Incubate the assembled constructs at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 days.
Prepare a cell suspension of tdTomato-expressing human adipose microvascular endothelial cells (HAMEC-tdTomato) at a concentration of 1 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Place a 20 µL droplet of the cell suspension on a hydrophobic surface.
Gently place vascular scaffolds on top of the droplet such that one end makes contact with the cell droplet.
Aspirate the droplet from the opposing end of the scaffold, filling its lumen with the cell suspension.
Place the seeded scaffold in a microcentrifuge tube and put it in a rotator inside a humidified incubator for 60 minutes.
Transfer the scaffold into a 12-well plate and add 2 mL of endothelial cell medium.
Culture the engineered flaps for 7 days, replacing the medium every 2 days with fresh endothelial cell medium.
Define fluorescence channels for ZsGreen1 and tdTomato fluorescent proteins on the microscope image acquisition software after 4 days and 7 days of culture.
Choose a 5x/0.16 objective lens with 0.5x zoom (pixel size 5 µm) and define a Z-stack with 22 slices, each with a thickness of 41 µm.
Define a 3 x 2 tile scan to image and capture the entire construct.
Adjust laser intensity and gain values to obtain a clear fluorescent signal with no saturation and minimal background.
Acquire images using the microscope image acquisition software or similar image analysis software.
Perform a maximum-intensity projection of the acquired Z-stack to obtain a single 2D image.
Perform higher magnification imaging of a region of interest.
Switch to a 10x/0.3 objective lens with 0.5 zoom (pixel size 1.25 µm).
Define a Z-stack with 9 slices of thicknesses of 41 µm.
Fix the engineered flaps by submerging them in 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 min after 7 days of culture.
Wash the constructs 3x 5 min with PBS.
Add 0.3% (v/v) Triton-X in PBS to the constructs and incubate for 15 min at room temperature to permeabilize the cells.
Wash the constructs 3x 5 min with PBS.
Prepare a blocking solution by dissolving 5% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS.
Add the blocking solution to the engineered flaps and incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting mouse anti-smooth muscle actin (anti-SMA) 1:50 antibody in the 5% BSA solution prepared previously.
Incubate the scaffolds in the primary antibody solution overnight at 4 °C.
Wash 3x 5 min with PBS.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution by diluting Cy3-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG 1:400 antibody and DAPI (2.5 µg/mL) in PBS.
Apply the secondary antibody solution to the scaffolds and incubate for 3 h at room temperature.
Wash 3x 5 min with PBS.
Store the constructs at 4 °C in PBS for up to 1 month.
Image the stained scaffolds using a confocal laser-scanning microscope.
Define the DAPI fluorescence channel on the microscope image acquisition software.
Define the ZsGreen fluorescence channel on the microscope image acquisition software.
Define the Cy3 fluorescence channel on the microscope image acquisition software.
Define a Z-stack with a section thickness of 2 µm spanning a total thickness of 50 µm.
Define a tile scan to image larger areas of the construct.
Adjust the acquisition parameters to obtain a clear fluorescent signal with no saturation and minimal background.
Acquire images using a 20x/0.8 objective with 1.0x zoom (pixel size 0.31 µm).
Perform a maximum-intensity projection of the acquired Z-stack to obtain a single 2D image using microscope image acquisition software or similar image analysis software.
Prepare and sterilize No. 15 scalpel, fine-toothed forceps, and small ring-handled scissors by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize straight fine-pointed No. 3 jeweler's forceps by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize angled jeweler's forceps by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize round-handled needle holder with curved jaws by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize vessel dilators by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize dissecting scissors by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize adventitia scissors by autoclaving.
Prepare and sterilize vessel clamps along with their applicator by autoclaving.
Dilute 5 mL of stock heparin solution with 195 mL of saline to prepare a solution of 100 IU/mL heparinized saline.
Cut sections of polyimide tube measuring 2.5 mm under a dissecting microscope.
Sterilize cut polyimide cuffs.
Make a 1.25 mm lengthwise incision in the wall of the tube at one end to obtain a cuff handle.
Make an angled cut at the other end of the tube to ease vessel eversion.
Submerge the cuffs in 70% ethanol.
Wash the cuffs twice with heparinized saline.
Begin administering subcutaneous daily dose of cyclosporine (10 mg kg-1) seven days prior to surgery.
Anesthetize the animal using 3% isoflurane inhalation according to institutional SOP using an induction chamber.
Verify deep anesthesia by pinching both feet and checking for reflexes.
Administer a subcutaneous dose of analgesic buprenorphine (0.03 mg kg-1).
Administer a subcutaneous dose of anticoagulative heparin (200 IU kg-1).
Apply a lubricating eye ointment to the animal's eyes to prevent dehydration.
Shave the surgical area of the rat.
Disinfect the surgical site with iodine.
Disinfect the surgical site with 70% ethanol.
Secure the animal's limbs to the table using adhesive tape.
Expose and isolate the common femoral artery.
Make a 2 cm long, oblique incision through the skin along the concavity between the leg and the abdomen.
Release the skin from the underlying tissue using forceps and blunt-ended scissors to visualize the inguinal fat pad.
Cut right through the fat pad around the upper, medial, and lower margins using scissors and forceps.
Pay attention not to cut large vessels underneath the fat pad.
Reflect the fat pad laterally, leaving the epigastric vessels intact.
Place a wet gauze on the reflected fat pad to prevent drying and fix it in place.
Expose the femoral artery from the inguinal ligament proximally to the epigastric artery branching point distally by extracting it from its sheath.
Divide the Murphy's branch by ligating it.
Ligate the femoral artery with two ligatures at the middle of the artery spaced 1 mm apart.
Cut the artery between the two ligatures using adventitia scissors.
Insert each vessel end into a polyimide cuff such that the two cuffs' handles are pointing away from each other.
Apply a clamp simultaneously on the cuff handle and the vessel, securing the cuff in place.
Prepare a heparinized saline solution in a syringe equipped with a 27 G needle.
Pull on the ligated vessel end and cut it close to the ligature.
Wash the vessel end thoroughly with heparinized saline until no blood is visible in the lumen.
Hold the vessel by its sheath with one hand and dilate its lumen with a vessel dilator with the other hand.
Place a loose 6-0 polypropylene circumferential suture around the cuff body.
Evert the vessel end using two vessel dilators over the cuff body.
Secure the everted vessel end in place by tightening the circumferential suture.
Rinse the engineered flap with heparinized saline if blood leaks during manipulations.
Insert the vessel-lined cuff into the lumen of the vascular scaffold.
Place a circumferential 6-0 polypropylene suture around the scaffold and the cuff body for both sides.
Wrap a 0.2 µm polystyrene membrane filter around the anastomoses site to isolate the engineered flap from surrounding tissue.
Release the distal clamp first, then release the proximal clamp to reestablish blood flow through the vessel.
Reflect the fat pad back over the femoral vessels.
Apply gentle pressure using a sterile gauze for 3 min.
Suture the fat pad in place using 6-0 polypropylene suture material.
Suture the skin using 5-0 PGA absorbable sutures.
Clean the wound area with saline solution.
Apply iodine solution to the wound area.
Prepare a 0.1% (v/v) tramadol solution in drinking water for postoperative pain management.
Administer heparin at a dose of 200 IU/kg daily.
Administer cyclosporine at a dose of 10 mg/kg daily.
Place the animal in a clean cage under a heating lamp.
Continue to monitor the animal until it regains sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
